```python
def rectangle_intersection_area(r1, r2):

    x2 = min(r1[2], r2[2])

```

The intersection of two rectangles is itself an axis-aligned rectangle. I compute its lower and upper coordinates by taking the maximum of the left sides and the minimum of the right sides along each axis, and do the same for the vertical sides. If the resulting left side of an axis is to the right of or equal to the right side (which can happen when rectangles touch along an edge), max(0, x2 - x1) becomes 0, and taking the product with the other axis gives 0, as the spec requires when rectangles do not overlap. Exactly one term can be negative only when both rectangles lie on opposite sides of a single axis and do not share any interior point, so the product can never be negative.
